subject: PromptWeave / Redwood - SDK integration pilot and SOW

Subject: Integration proposal - PromptWeave + Redwood

Hi Mina,

Great to connect last week at the partner summit. PromptWeave builds a prompt orchestration and evaluation SDK that a lot of ISVs embed in their stack; we're exploring a formal integration with Redwood to offer an out-of-the-box connector for LangChain and LlamaIndex users and optional tracing passthrough for observability.

High-level asks:
- Official adapter packages (LangChain / LlamaIndex) that call Redwood endpoints with token attribution.
- An optional trace propagation pattern (traceparent + span) so customers can see end-to-end traces across SDK and the Redwood runtime.
- A basic joint SOW for a 6-week pilot to validate throughput and error-handling.

I've attached a short proposal and a rough one-pager (PW-Redwood-Integration-Proposal.pdf). Can you point me to the right technical contact on Redwood to scope tracing details and an initial SOW?

Thanks,
Elena Brooks
Head of Partnerships, PromptWeave

Subject: Re: Integration proposal - Integration details and requirements

Thanks for the quick response — we can do Fri 8/23 9am PT; sent calendar invite.

To help the call, a short list of integration requirements and constraints:
- LangChain: we want an official connector that accepts PromptWeave run metadata and forwards generation calls to Redwood with a customer-scoped API key.
- LlamaIndex: need a document-store connector that can pull embeddings from Redwood and optionally push vector updates.
- Tracing: prefer W3C traceparent propagation. We want the SDK wrapper to attach traceparent and parent-span-id so traces correlate across SDK -> Redwood.
- Security: customers expect per-tenant key isolation and explicit audit log entries for token usage.
- Pilot success criteria: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for short chat prompts (<=256 tokens); no functional regressions in prompt completions; integrated trace view showing end-to-end span for at least 3 demo apps.

Budget note: PromptWeave can commit to a paid pilot. We're expecting an SOW and a simple PO/DocuSign flow.

Attached: integration-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet with sample payloads and trace examples).

Samir
CTO, PromptWeave
Attachments: integration-requirements.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@promptweave.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Integration proposal - Integration details and requirements

Samir / Elena — thanks for the worksheet, that's very helpful. A few clarifications and a proposal from our side:

1) Tracing approaches (tradeoffs)
- SDK-side trace wrapper: PromptWeave can add a small wrapper in the SDK that attaches the W3C traceparent header and a PromptWeave span id. Pros: minimal runtime changes on Redwood and full visibility inside the SDK. Cons: requires SDK updates across LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters.
- Server-side tracehook: Redwood can accept an optional trace context field in the request body and synthesize spans server-side, attaching Redwood span ids that correlate. Pros: no mandatory SDK changes for customers; Cons: slightly less granularity for SDK-local spans.

We can support both patterns. For the pilot I recommend implementing the SDK-side wrapper for LangChain (fast path) and the server-side tracehook as a fallback for older SDK versions.

2) Auth / key attribution
- Recommend per-customer API keys with token attribution header (X-Redwood-Client) included by the SDK connector. We'll send a short spec for the header and token rotation APIs.

3) Performance and batching
- We observed that continuous batching can improve throughput but increases tail latency for single-shot prompts. For your 95th < 300ms target, we suggest conservative batching for the pilot (max batch delay 20ms) and sample-based KV cache warming for the LlamaIndex connector.

4) Pilot scope and timeline
- Week 0: Kickoff and final SOW sign-off
- Weeks 1-3: Implement LangChain adapter + SDK wrapper; Redwood provides a trace test harness and a sandbox account
- Weeks 4-5: Integration testing + performance tuning
- Week 6: Demo and handoff; collect telemetry to validate SLOs

Estimated work: Redwood engineering ~3 engineer-weeks (adapter + trace support + test harness). Ballpark pilot cost estimate: $18k-$25k depending on support level.

Attachments: redwood-trace-adapter-design.md (technical notes w/ sample pseudocode).

Can you confirm: (a) you accept the two-pattern tracing approach, (b) pilot budget range, (c) who signs the SOW on your side?

—Marcus
Senior Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-trace-adapter-design.md

Thanks Marcus — that approach looks good to us. PromptWeave accepts the dual-pattern tracing plan: SDK wrapper as the preferred path plus server-side tracehook fallback. Budget range and timeline look fine.

Action items from our side:
- Legal will review the SOW; our ops lead (Samir) will coordinate PO and DocuSign.
- We have a small redline request on data retention: prefer 90 days for pilot logs vs the 180 listed in your draft. We'll send a redline to LegalOps in the next 24 hours.

Next steps from Redwood: please send the initial SOW (PW-Redwood-SOW-v1.pdf) to DocuSign and share the sandbox credentials and the Drive folder you mentioned. Proposed kickoff: Mon 8/31 9am PT.
